title: Fully integrating the Flang Fortran compiler with standard MLIR
problem: Flang's Fortran compiler does not fully integrate with MLIR, instead using bespoke translation and optimization passes to target LLVM-IR. This fragmented approach prevents leveraging standard MLIR infrastructure and limits performance optimization opportunities.
motivation: Fortran is critical for HPC application development, making it essential to have efficient open-source Fortran compilers that generate high-performance executables.
method: The authors develop a direct mapping between Fortran language constructs and standard MLIR dialects to replace Flang's custom passes. They benchmark this new mapping against Flang's existing approach and other HPC compilers, measuring performance improvements through leveraging MLIR's unified optimization infrastructure and standard dialects.
key_novelty: Direct mapping of Fortran to standard MLIR dialects, eliminating custom translation passes in favor of reusable MLIR infrastructure.
contributions: Formal Fortran-to-standard-MLIR mapping eliminating bespoke compiler passes
Up to 3x performance improvement compared to Flang's existing approach
Validation that standard MLIR can effectively replace domain-specific optimizations
Performance comparison across HPC compiler ecosystem

metrics.speedup: up to 3x over Flang's existing approach
